files.purpose: Defines ChatBadge, the generic tinted pill used in the conversation (glyph, one-line title, optional caption, optional chevron) whose click toggles a bound isPresented flag, and which can run an inverted accent dot-field wave across its top quarter when needsAttention is true. It also defines the anchored-popover machinery every chat pill shares: the View.badgePopover(isPresented:detail:) modifier for pills that draw themselves, and BadgePopoverCoordinator, an NSPopover wrapper that measures the detail once with NSHostingView.fittingSize, freezes that size, hangs it from the pill's window rect, and closes it on Escape (keyCode 53) in the owning window or popover, or on a left/right mouse-down in the owning window outside the pill's rect.

side_effects: Showing a popover installs two app-local NSEvent monitors: one for .keyDown (Escape) and one for [.leftMouseDown, .rightMouseDown]; they are removed on close() and again in popoverDidClose
The Escape monitor swallows the event (returns nil) after closing; the mouse-down monitor closes the popover but passes the event through (returns event)

feature_notes: The order of modifiers in ChatBadge.body is: Button -> .buttonStyle(.plain) -> .disabled(!isEnabled) -> dot overlay -> .clipShape -> .windowRectAnchor -> .onChange(of: isPresented) -> .onAppear -> .onDisappear -> .frame(maxWidth: .infinity, alignment: .leading) -> .padding(.trailing, 96) -> accessibility. The anchor rect is therefore the clipped pill, before the full-width frame.

isPresented true: if the coordinator is not already shown, coordinator.show(detail().presentedChrome()). isPresented false: coordinator.close(). The observer is `.onChange(of: isPresented) { _, shown in ... }` (line 67, and line 101 in BadgePopoverModifier) without `initial: true`, so a badge that mounts with isPresented already true does not open its popover until the flag changes.

show(): `guard let anchor = anchorRect.flatMap(WindowRectAnchor.target(for:)) else { return }` (line 139) returns silently when anchorRect is nil or WindowRectAnchor.target(for:) returns nil; isPresented, already toggled true by the button (line 23 `isPresented.toggle()`), stays true, so the next click only toggles it back to false (close() is a no-op because nothing is shown) and a third click is needed to try again. If a popover is still shown it is closed at once (unreachable from the two callers, see side_effects). The content gets .environment(\.closePopover, { [weak self] in self?.close() }) so rows or sheets inside can close it. Size is NSHostingView(rootView: content).fittingSize, replaced by 460 x 320 if either side is <= 0, then popover.setFixedContent(content, size: size). shownIn = anchor.view.window; shownRect = anchor.view.convert(anchor.rect, to: nil). Shown with preferredEdge .minY if anchor.view.isFlipped else .maxY. Then startMonitors().
close(): no-op unless popover.isShown; stops monitors then popover.performClose(nil) (animated). onClose runs from popoverDidClose once, whichever way the popover closed.

startMonitors(): guarded by monitors.isEmpty. Escape (keyCode 53) is only handled when event.window is the shown-in chat window or the popover's own window; Escape in another window (the comment names Settings and a file picker) is left alone.

handleMouseDown: ignores events whose window is not shownIn; a click inside shownRect (the badge itself) passes through without closing, so the badge's own toggle handles it; any other click in that window closes the popover and still delivers the event.

badgePopover(isPresented:detail:) duplicates ChatBadge's popover wiring (windowRectAnchor, onChange, onAppear onClose, onDisappear close) for pills that draw themselves, wrapping the detail in AnyView.

Int ?? Int ?? 100)`, doc comment at :251-252 'The app-wide zoom in percent: the whole window scales, the way a browser's zoom does, rather than the conversation's type alone.', applied in WindowManager.swift:175 `.modifier(AppZoomModifier(percent: model.settings.appZoom))`, driven by the menu items 'Zoom In' (Cmd-+ and Cmd-=), 'Zoom Out' (Cmd--) and 'Actual Size' (Cmd-0, sets 100) in AppCommands.swift:53-61 and the Settings row ChromeRow(title: "Zoom") in SettingsView.swift:469; ChatFont.swift:5 says 'The app-wide zoom scales the window, not the type.' files.purpose: ChatView is the chat column for one ThreadRuntime: the per-thread ThreadTimeline (swapped by .id(runtime.threadID)) with the ComposerArea inset at its bottom, the sticky glass ChatChromeRow on top, up to five kinds of floating docked panels (helper/subagent, Hydra team, popped-out head, auto-popped heads, usage) laid out in corners with drag-to-dock, live slot reordering and grip resizing persisted to Settings, and the optional TerminalPanel below. The file also holds the panel geometry engine (PanelMembers, PanelScene with its Geometry, slot ordering and stack-depth rules), the ReserveSlide modifier that makes room for docked panels without relayout per frame, the Jump-to-latest button, the git status model with a 30 second per-directory snapshot cache, and the chrome-row menus and sheets (thread title copy/rename, threads popover, permissions, branch switch/create/worktree, Open in, project scripts and their editor, commit/push/pull request and the commit sheet with generated messages).

feature_notes: Body order: thread = model.thread(runtime.threadID); project; workingDirectory = thread.worktreePath ?? project.path; directory = workingDirectory ?? LoginEnvironment.homeDirectory; title = thread?.title ?? ""; members = PanelMembers(...); scene = PanelScene(..., holdsHydra: hydraLingers, preferredSize: livePreferredSize, usageHeightOverride: panelResize.liveUsageHeight); hydraPresent = !members.heads.isEmpty && scene.isMeasured; switching = sceneThreadID != runtime.threadID.

ThreadTimeline gets supportsRewind = thread?.provider.supportsRewind ?? false, hit testing off while isMovingAPanel, .id(runtime.threadID), and ReserveSlide with slides = scene.isMeasured && !liveResize.isActive && !holds && !switching. The composer gets the same ReserveSlide with animatesWidth: true.
Composer growth: onChange(of: composerAreaHeight) calls scrollState.noteComposerAreaGrowth() only when newValue > oldValue + 0.5, liveResize is not active and oldValue > 0.

Hydra linger: on HydraPresence change, a thread change resets lingers and sets hydraShownSince to now when present; present sets hydraShownSince = now and lingers false; absent while runtime.isHydraPanelHidden drops lingers; otherwise if the panel was shown for less than 1.6 s, hydraLingers = true and a MainActor task sleeps the remaining seconds and then sets hydraLingers = false with Chrome.panelSlide. Hiding the panel via the Hydra button while it lingers cancels the task and ends the linger with Chrome.panelSlide.

Live resize: while liveResize.isActive, each paneSize change reclamps every drag state (subagent, hydra, popped, usage, each autoDrag) in scene.layout; when the live resize ends they reclamp once more. autoDrags gets a PanelDragState per auto-popped head id and loses ids no longer present (initial: true).

Thread switch (onChange runtime.threadID): sceneThreadID updated, linger cancelled and cleared, fresh ChromeScrollModel, TimelineScrollState, all PanelDragStates, autoDrags = [:], PanelResizeState. onAppear sets sceneThreadID. All panel animations use nil while switching.
mergeRequestTarget environment: MergeRequestTarget(chatID: runtime.threadID) whose action calls model.spawnSubagent(from: runtime.threadID, title: link.title, prompt: link.prompt).

Subagent panel: default slot corner runtime.subagentPanelDock; workingDirectory is subagent.worktreePath ?? project?.path; close runs model.closeSubagent(subagent.id) inside withAnimation(Chrome.panelSlide). Drag calls dock then reorder on every move and on release (release() returns the heading position). Its grip is `resize: resizer(for: runtime.subagentPanelDock, scene: scene)` (line 355), the stored dock, whereas the Hydra (line 396, `corner` = slot.corner from line 361), popped (line 450, `corner` = slot.corner from line 422), auto-popped (line 485 `slot.corner`) and usage (line 527, `corner = slot.corner` from line 493) panels use their slot's corner; in a narrow pane the helper's slot corner can be rewritten to the other side (line 992) while its grip signs (acrossSign, downSign, lines 540-541) still follow runtime.subagentPanelDock.

Hydra panel: popOut(id) sets hydraPoppedHeadID = id, hydraPoppedPanelDock = hydraPanelDock.acrossTheColumn and clears hydraSelectedHeadID if it was that id; dismiss calls model.dismissHydraHeads(of:). The panel gets .id(runtime.threadID) and HydraCaptureFrame, which records the global frame into WebsiteCaptures.hydraPanelFrames only when captures are enabled and no live resize is running.

Popped panel: HydraPanel(heads: [popped], isPoppedOut: true); dismiss sets hydraSelectedHeadID = popped.id and hydraPoppedHeadID = nil; .id(popped.id). Auto-popped panel: default corner hydraPanelDock.acrossTheColumn; drag state autoDrags[head.id] ?? autoDrag; dismiss inserts head.id into hydraAutoPopHeld and selects it; .id(head.id).

Usage panel: height = scene.usageHeight ?? full height; bottom-docked panels shift origin down by (full.height - height) so the bottom edge stays; content height reports update usageContentHeight only when different; dismiss sets model.settings.showsUsagePanel = false for every chat.

resizer: panelResize.begin(at: layout.panelSize); width sign -1 for a trailing corner, height sign -1 for a bottom corner; liveSize = layout.fitted(next); onReset sets settings.panelSize = nil with Chrome.panelSlide. usageResizer: width like resizer; height liveUsageHeight = max(minimum, start.height + dy * sign); onReset sets settings.usagePanelHeight = nil. commitPanelResize writes the live values to settings once, clears them and ends. livePreferredSize rounds live width to a multiple of 12 while a grip is held.

dock(): wanted = layout.dockCorner(nearest:keeping: current, docks:); if scene.lockedSide(excluding: id) is non-nil the corner is forced onto that side keeping top/bottom; written only when changed. dockUsage writes settings.usagePanelDock the same way; dockAuto writes hydraAutoPanelDocks[id], starting from the stored dock, then the slot's corner, then hydraPanelDock.acrossTheColumn.
lockedSide: nil when layout.fitsBothSides or no other panel; the Hydra panel's side if it is among the others; else leading when leading count >= trailing count, otherwise trailing.

reorder(): n = max(slotsOnSide[side] ?? 1, others.count + 1); target = layout.slotIndex(at:slots:docks:); slot index is below for top corners and n - 1 - below for bottom corners; previous = the panel's own index if its current slot is on this side. `let full = !(others.count + 1 > (scene.slotsOnSide[side] ?? 1))` (line 650) and `if let other = occupancy[target], previous != nil, full` swaps: occupancy[previous!] = other, occupancy[target] = id. Because slotsOnSide[side] = max(natural, placed count on side) (line 1012) and a panel with previous != nil is itself counted on that side, `full` is always true when previous != nil, so the swap happens whenever the target slot is occupied and the panel already had a slot on this side, even with free slots on the side (the comment at lines 636-639 'a taken one on a full side is swapped' does not match the executed test). Otherwise, if the target is occupied, the occupant and the following ones shift one slot in the drag direction (forward when previous == nil or previous < target); if the chain runs off an end, `forward ? (0..<n).first(where: { occupancy[$0] == nil }) : (0..<n).reversed().first(where: { occupancy[$0] == nil })` (line 662): running off the high end forward wraps to the lowest free index, running off index 0 backward wraps to the highest free index, i.e. the opposite end from where it ran off (the displaced panel is dropped from occupancy if no slot is free). A free target is simply taken. The corners are rewritten via PanelDocks.corner(forSlot:of:side:) and panelStackOrder becomes the other panels (kept, minus this side's and id) followed by this side's top panels in ascending slot index then bottom panels in descending slot index; written only if changed.
rest(for:): scene.docks.stacked(corner, below:, slots: slotsOnSide[side] ?? 1, layout:), then y + lift for top corners, y - lift for bottom corners.

ReserveSlide: sets reserveSlideLeading = reserve.leading and reserveSlideOffset = offset, pads leading/trailing by the reserve, animates the padding with Chrome.panelSlide only when animatesWidth && slides, offsets x by offset; on reserve change the shift is ((new.leading - new.trailing) - (old.leading - old.trailing)) / 2; when slides, !animatesWidth and shift != 0 the offset jumps by -shift in a transaction with animations disabled and then animates back to 0 with Chrome.panelSlide, otherwise offset = 0.

PanelMembers: subagent = model.panelSubagent(of:); heads come from model.panelHeads(of:) unless runtime.isHydraPanelHidden (then []); popped is the head with id hydraPoppedHeadID only when the team has more than one head; heads exclude the popped one; usage exists only when `if let thread = model.thread(runtime.threadID), model.settings.showsUsagePanel` (line 797) holds, i.e. the thread must exist and settings.showsUsagePanel be true, with headsProvider = model.hydraHeadsProvider(of: pair) when Hydra is on for the thread and that provider differs from the thread's. PanelScene.heads is `members.heads.filter { head in !geometry.autoPopped.contains { $0.id == head.id } }` (line 887), and it is what the team panel gets (`heads: scene.heads`, line 365), so the team panel also drops the auto-popped heads.

Geometry: isMeasured = paneSize != .zero; preferred = preferredSize ?? settings.panelSize; showsHydra = (heads non-empty || holdsHydra) && isMeasured; showsPopped = popped != nil && showsHydra; showsUsage = usage != nil && isMeasured; compact = !settings.hydraShowsHeadDetails && (members.subagent?.isHydraHead ?? true) && (showsHydra || subagent != nil). Placement order: subagent, hydra, popped, usage. Usage height = min(max(usageMinimumHeight, room), max(usageMinimumHeight, wanted)) where room = single.verticalRoom - below * (slotHeight + gap) and wanted = override ?? settings.usagePanelHeight ?? usageContentHeight ?? slotHeight; usageLift = max(0, usageHeight - slotHeight). Ordering: `let under = Self.order(placed, by: runtime.panelStackOrder)[.usage]?.below ?? 0` (line 947) is computed when placed holds only subagent, hydra, popped and usage at their stored docks (lines 940-943), before auto-popped heads are appended (lines 962-983) and before the narrow-pane side forcing (lines 987-994), so the usage height cap ignores auto-popped panels stacked under it and any forced side change.

Slots per side: natural = min(3, max(1, Int((verticalRoom + gap) / (smallest + gap)))) with smallest = compactHeight when compact else minHeight. Auto-pop (settings.hydraAutoPopsHeads, showsHydra, more than one head): candidates are heads after the first not in hydraAutoPopHeld; ones with a stored hydraAutoPanelDocks entry are placed there first; the rest fill free slots in corners [hydraPanelDock.acrossTheColumn, hydraPanelDock] (only [hydraPanelDock] when both sides do not fit), counting both corners of a side plus ceil(usageLift / (slotHeight + gap)) extra when the usage panel is on that side.

Narrow pane (!fitsBothSides) with panels on both sides: all go to the Hydra panel's side, else the fuller side (ties to leading), keeping top/bottom (line 992 `placed = placed.map { ($0.id, PanelDockCorner.make(side: home, isTop: $0.corner.isTop)) }`). Lift applies to panels in the usage panel's corner stacked beyond it: `if let usageBelow, entry.corner == usageCorner, showsUsage, id != .usage, entry.below > usageBelow` (line 1000), where `let usageCorner = model.settings.usagePanelDock` is captured at line 944, before the narrow-pane rewrite; when the usage panel is forced to the other side, the panels stacked beyond it on the new side no longer match usageCorner and get no lift. slotsOnSide[side] = max(natural, placed on side). stackDepth: for each side with more than one occupied slot, depth = ceil((n - 1) / closest gap) + 1, the maximum across sides. Reserve per side = layout.composerReserve when that side has a panel.
order(): ranks by first appearance in panelStackOrder (unranked = Int.max), ties by placement order, per corner; below = index in that sorted list.

GitStatusModel.refresh: applies a cached snapshot immediately; returns without running git when !force and the snapshot is under 30 s old; else reads isRepository, and when a repository runs status, branches and remoteWebURL concurrently, stores and applies. perform() sets activity to the given label for the duration and returns the thrown error or nil.

Git actions: switchBranch label "Switching", error alert "Could not switch branch"; createBranch trims whitespace and newlines, replaces spaces with "-", ignores empty, label "Creating", error "Could not create branch"; push label "Pushing", error "Push failed"; PR label "Opening pull request": push, then subject from git log -1 --pretty=%s and body from --pretty=%b (both trimmed, failures become ""), createPullRequest(title: subject or "Update", body: body or "Opened from Droppy Code."), error "Could not open a pull request", success opens the URL. Every action refreshes git afterwards. Alert messages are error.localizedDescription.

CommitSheet: `.task { let changes = await Git(directory).workingChanges(); summary = changes.summary; if message.isEmpty { await generate(changes: changes) } }` (lines 1605-1609; a .task, so cancelled when the sheet goes away, not an onAppear) loads the working changes, shows the summary and auto-generates when message is empty. generate returns immediately with no text engine (model.textEngine(preferring: runtime.thread?.provider)); calls TextGeneration.commitMessage with settings.commitInstructions and the directory URL; a nil result leaves the message unchanged. commit: label "Committing", commitAll(message: trimmed), then push if the toggle was on; refresh; error alert "Commit failed" keeps the sheet, success dismisses.

Doc comments at lines 53-57 (hydraShownSince) and 713-720 (ReserveSlide) sit above other declarations (panelsHeld and HydraPresence respectively) in the source; this is layout of comments only.

B1->B2: (1) ChatView.body lost the .environment(\.chatZoom, ChatZoom.scale(at: model.settings.chatZoom)) modifier and its 3-line comment after .id(runtime.threadID), so the timeline no longer receives a separate conversation text-size factor (chatZoom is absent from all of DroppyCode at B2). B2 does not drop text scaling, it moves it: B1's chatZoom was one global AppSettings value (B1 AppSettings.swift:130 `static let chatZoom = "chatZoom"`, :709 `chatZoom = ChatZoom.clamped(defaults.object(forKey: Key.chatZoom) as? Int ?? ChatZoom.defaultIndex)`), not stored per thread; the removed B1 ChatView comment called it 'The text size set in Settings, for the conversation alone: the row and the chat box keep their own size.' B2 replaces it with the app-wide window zoom appZoom: AppSettings.swift:131 `static let appZoom = "appZoom"`, :718 `appZoom = AppZoom.normalized(defaults.object(forKey: Key.appZoom) as? Int ?? 100)`, doc comment at :251-252 'The app-wide zoom in percent: the whole window scales, the way a browser's zoom does, rather than the conversation's type alone.', applied in WindowManager.swift:175 `.modifier(AppZoomModifier(percent: model.settings.appZoom))`, driven by the menu items 'Zoom In' (Cmd-+ and Cmd-=), 'Zoom Out' (Cmd--) and 'Actual Size' (Cmd-0, sets 100) in AppCommands.swift:53-61 and the Settings row ChromeRow(title: "Zoom") in SettingsView.swift:469; ChatFont.swift:5 says 'The app-wide zoom scales the window, not the type.' So the port keeps a whole-window zoom rather than removing scaling. (2) Fixed point sizes became text styles: ChatChromeTitle .system(size: 15, weight: .semibold) -> .system(.title3, weight: .semibold); CommitSheet title .system(size: 17, weight: .semibold) -> .system(.title2, weight: .semibold), summary .system(size: 11, design: .monospaced) -> .system(.subheadline, design: .monospaced), TextEditor .system(size: 13) -> .system(.body); ScriptsEditor title size 17 semibold -> .title2 semibold, description .system(size: 12) -> .system(.callout), Command field .system(size: 12, design: .monospaced) -> .system(.callout, design: .monospaced). (3) trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespacesAndNewlines) was replaced by the String.trimmed helper (same semantics, Text.swift:132) in createBranch, both git log reads in openPullRequest, the Commit button's disabled check and commit(). ScriptsEditor.isIncomplete keeps trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespaces). Diff: 12 insertions, 16 deletions; no strings, symbols or logic changed otherwise.
unresolved_questions: Whether the B2 text styles render at exactly the old fixed sizes on macOS (title3 15, title2 17, subheadline 11, body 13, callout 12 are the usual macOS defaults) is not established by this file; a reference capture or Apple's type table should confirm before the port fixes pixel sizes.
